sections.html:
Grady County sits on Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo, the seat, is also the biggest city, and only Cairo and Whigham are incorporated. All parcels share one county digest while cities may add a levy of their own, so study each line of your bill before agreeing to a price.

The 2020 census counted 26,236 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 26,590 is a 1.4% increase. About 21.2% of residents are 65 or older, so age-based exemptions matter to many owners thinking of a move. Builders took out just 55 permits in 2025, which means resale homes dominate the market.

One middle figure says little about a single parcel. Trust the value on your assessment notice, and if taxes are behind, get a payoff number from the commissioner before choosing how to sell.

sections.h2: Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?
sections.html:
Two offices divide the work. The tax commissioner's side bills land, buildings, business property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber. The Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser, deals with returns, values and conservation or agricultural applications.

  • Tax commissioner: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open Monday to Thursday from half past seven in the morning until six in the evening and closed Fridays.
  • Tax commissioner and assessor service pages: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site has a search tool covering each parcel.

Call 229-377-3322 before you go, to confirm where to pay and the current hours. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

The taxable base is 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and each yearly notice prints both figures. If you think the value is high, write to the Board of Tax Assessors. Your letter needs a postmark within 45 days of the date the notice went out. On state form PT-311A you choose where the case goes: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator.

A revaluation year can push notices, and their deadlines, later than usual, so rely on the dates printed on your notice, not on last year's calendar. File a copy of the notice and your appeal letter in the folder you hand the title company. They will ask which value your bill rests on.

Statewide, the default deadline is December 20. Grady officials may choose December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments. Your printed bill shows the date that counts. Interest stays off for 60 days after the postmark, and unpaid balances can pick up penalties after that.

If a parcel is already overdue, ask the commissioner for the penalty and interest owed. Three other fixed points apply here:

  • Returns for property you held on January 1 are accepted from that day through April 1.
  • A mobile home in the county on January 1 needs a tax return by April 1, filed alongside its location permit.
  • For tax assessed or collected wrongly, the refund claim must begin within three years of paying.

A homestead application can go in any time after you move in, and April 1 is the last day for the first year. Under state rules a missed filing counts as a waiver. The standard state deduction takes $2,000 off assessed value, and the assessor can say whether local amounts stack on top.

In early 2025 the county commissioners announced plans to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption. Check with the assessor before telling a buyer the value is frozen.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters adopted it, with filing on the return schedule.
  • A buyer files separately, since an exemption does not pass with the deed.

A November 2026 county notice shows a tentative millage rate that raises property taxes by 4.72 percent. The tentative rate is 12.64 mills, up .57 mill from 12.070 mills, the most the county could set without the increase. The notice gave hearing dates at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo.

That figure covers only the county's own levy. School and city rates come separately, and the final numbers show on your bill. Ask the commissioner's office for the rates that apply to your parcel when you need a payoff figure.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Sell faster by having the paperwork ready: the latest tax bill, the assessment notice showing its mailing date, and any appeal letter you sent. If you applied for conservation use or an agricultural assessment, add that application, because a buyer will ask whether the land stays enrolled.

Next, phone the commissioner at 229-377-3322 for the balance on the current year and every earlier one. A recorded execution blocks a closing until it is satisfied. Cairo and Whigham may bill separately, so check with each city office too. With 66.1% of housing owner-occupied and few new builds, a clean tax record helps your house stand out among resale listings.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is liable for that year's entire bill. Even a sale on January 2 leaves it that way, with nothing refunded by the state. The buyer and seller split the cost through the contract, and the settlement statement shows the result.

  • Ask the commissioner what the parcel owes now and for prior years.
  • Warn your closing agent about any open appeal, because a corrected bill may follow.
  • Give the agent the payoff amount and the office that receives it.
  • Notify the office when your homestead exemption ends because you moved.

Even a buyer who takes the house as-is for cash inherits the parcel with its tax history. Any back taxes belong on the settlement statement and are paid from your proceeds, so get the figure in writing early.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. One page gives 114 1st Street NE with Monday to Thursday hours, and the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of eight to five. Call 229-377-3322 first to learn which counter takes payment.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?
faqs.a: 45 days from the mailing date. Postmark your letter inside that period, address it to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

faqs.q: Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The state's standard $2,000 exemption applies. Because of the county's 2025 plan to opt out of the base year freeze, ask the assessor which rules cover your home now.

faqs.q: If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner owes it, and no part of the year is refunded. Your contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before closing.

faqs.q: Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?
faqs.a: Yes, when the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. The request must be in writing and made within three years of payment. If the assessment is under appeal, the refund follows once the final taxable value is set.
